claim: Atherosclerosis is characterized by the formation of fibrofatty lesions in the arterial wall.
source: Atherosclerosis, characterized by the formation of fibrofatty lesions in the arterial wall, is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, contributing to most myocardial infarctions and many strokes (Herrington et al., 2016; Libby et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Herrington et al., 2016 and Libby et al., 2019, indicating established scientific knowledge.

claim: Atherosclerosis is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide.
source: Atherosclerosis, characterized by the formation of fibrofatty lesions in the arterial wall, is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, contributing to most myocardial infarctions and many strokes (Herrington et al., 2016; Libby et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Herrington et al., 2016 and Libby et al., 2019.

claim: Atherosclerosis contributes to most myocardial infarctions and many strokes.
source: Atherosclerosis, characterized by the formation of fibrofatty lesions in the arterial wall, is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, contributing to most myocardial infarctions and many strokes (Herrington et al., 2016; Libby et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Herrington et al., 2016 and Libby et al., 2019.

claim: The activation of vascular endothelial cells is an initial step in the development of atherosclerosis.
source: The activation of vascular endothelial cells (ECs), induced by various chemical and mechanical stimuli, such as lipopolysaccharide and shear stress, is an initial step in the development of atherosclerosis (Davignon and Ganz, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Davignon and Ganz, 2004.

claim: Atherosclerotic lesions preferentially develop at the branches and curvatures of the arterial tree, where blood flow is disturbed.
source: Consequently, atherosclerotic lesions preferentially develop at the branches and curvatures of the arterial tree, where blood flow is disturbed (Davis et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Davis et al., 2023.

claim: Yap/Taz is a mechanosensitive protein that regulates disturbed shear stress in endothelial cells.
source: Several mechanosensitive proteins, such as Yap/Taz (Li et al., 2019), Annexin A2 (Zhang et al., 2020), Bmp4 (Sorescu et al., 2004), and Nad(p)h oxidase (Hwang et al., 2003; Jo et al., 2006), have been identified as key regulators of disturbed shear stress in ECs and have been implicated in the progression of atherosclerosis.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Li et al., 2019.

claim: Annexin A2 is a mechanosensitive protein that regulates disturbed shear stress in endothelial cells.
source: Several mechanosensitive proteins, such as Yap/Taz (Li et al., 2019), Annexin A2 (Zhang et al., 2020), Bmp4 (Sorescu et al., 2004), and Nad(p)h oxidase (Hwang et al., 2003; Jo et al., 2006), have been identified as key regulators of disturbed shear stress in ECs and have been implicated in the progression of atherosclerosis.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2020.

claim: Bmp4 is a mechanosensitive protein that regulates disturbed shear stress in endothelial cells.
source: Several mechanosensitive proteins, such as Yap/Taz (Li et al., 2019), Annexin A2 (Zhang et al., 2020), Bmp4 (Sorescu et al., 2004), and Nad(p)h oxidase (Hwang et al., 2003; Jo et al., 2006), have been identified as key regulators of disturbed shear stress in ECs and have been implicated in the progression of atherosclerosis.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sorescu et al., 2004.

claim: Nad(p)h oxidase is a mechanosensitive protein that regulates disturbed shear stress in endothelial cells.
source: Several mechanosensitive proteins, such as Yap/Taz (Li et al., 2019), Annexin A2 (Zhang et al., 2020), Bmp4 (Sorescu et al., 2004), and Nad(p)h oxidase (Hwang et al., 2003; Jo et al., 2006), have been identified as key regulators of disturbed shear stress in ECs and have been implicated in the progression of atherosclerosis.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hwang et al., 2003 and Jo et al., 2006.

claim: Pharmacological or genetic inhibition of endothelial Yap activation ameliorates the progression of atherosclerotic plaques in mice.
source: Emerging evidence has revealed that pharmacological or genetic inhibition of endothelial Yap activation ameliorates the progression of atherosclerotic plaques in mice (Li et al., 2019; Wang et al., 2016; Yang et al., 2021), indicating that targeting disturbed flow-induced endothelial activation could be a promising therapeutic strategy for atherosclerosis.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Li et al., 2019, Wang et al., 2016, and Yang et al., 2021.

claim: The interferon regulatory factor (IRF) family comprises nine members (Irf1-Irf9) in mammals.
source: The interferon regulatory factor (IRF) family of transcription factors, comprising nine members (Irf1-Irf9) in mammals, is primarily characterized by its role in mediating antiviral responses and type I interferon production (Sato et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sato et al., 2001.

claim: Irf5 plays a central role in inflammation.
source: Although these members share a conserved DNA-binding domain in their N-terminal region that recognizes similar DNA sequences, Irf5 plays a central role in inflammation (Almuttaqi and Udalova, 2019; Takaoka et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Almuttaqi and Udalova, 2019 and Takaoka et al., 2005.

claim: Irf5 mediates the production of proinflammatory cytokines, including Il12b and Il23a.
source: Irf5 mediates the production of proinflammatory cytokines, including Il12b and Il23a, and promotes the expression of inflammatory genes (Cai et al., 2017; Saliba et al., 2014; Weiss et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cai et al., 2017, Saliba et al., 2014, and Weiss et al., 2013.

claim: Irf5 promotes inflammatory responses in macrophages.
source: It promotes inflammatory responses in various immune cells, including macrophages (Seneviratne et al., 2017), neutrophils (Weiss et al., 2015), and B cells (Savitsky et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Seneviratne et al., 2017.

claim: Irf5 promotes inflammatory responses in neutrophils.
source: It promotes inflammatory responses in various immune cells, including macrophages (Seneviratne et al., 2017), neutrophils (Weiss et al., 2015), and B cells (Savitsky et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Weiss et al., 2015.

claim: Irf5 promotes inflammatory responses in B cells.
source: It promotes inflammatory responses in various immune cells, including macrophages (Seneviratne et al., 2017), neutrophils (Weiss et al., 2015), and B cells (Savitsky et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Savitsky et al., 2010.

claim: Global or myeloid-specific knockouts of Irf5 exert anti-atherosclerotic effects.
source: Global or myeloid-specific knockouts of Irf5 have been shown to exert anti-atherosclerotic effects (Leipner et al., 2021; Seneviratne et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Leipner et al., 2021 and Seneviratne et al., 2017.

claim: Aff3ir contributes to endothelial maintenance by promoting the differentiation of vascular stem/progenitor cells (SPCs) into ECs.
source: We recently reported that a novel protein-coding nested gene, Aff3ir, contributes to endothelial maintenance by promoting the differentiation of vascular stem/progenitor cells (SPCs) into ECs (Zhao et al., 2025).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zhao et al., 2025.

claim: Aff3ir-ORF2 is predominantly expressed in the EC layer of the mouse aorta.
source: Aff3ir-ORF2, encoded by the Aff3ir transcript variant 2, is predominantly expressed in the EC layer of the mouse aorta (Zhao et al., 2025).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zhao et al., 2025.

claim: Overexpression of Aff3ir-ORF2 enhances laminar flow-induced mRNA levels of essential EC markers in SPCs.
source: Notably, our recent study indicated that the overexpression of Aff3ir-ORF2 could enhance laminar flow-induced mRNA levels of essential EC markers in SPCs (Zhao et al., 2025), suggesting that Aff3ir-ORF2 may be a novel mechanotransduction protein in ECs.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zhao et al., 2025.

claim: The mRNA level of Aff3ir is significantly lower in the intima of the aortic arch compared to the intima of the thoracic aorta.
source: We found that the mRNA level of Aff3ir, but not its parent gene Aff3, was significantly lower in the intima of the aortic arch, an area exposed to disturbed shear stress, compared to the intima of the thoracic aorta, which was exposed to steady unidirectional shear stress (Li et al., 2019; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1A and citation to Li et al., 2019.

claim: The expression of Aff3ir-ORF2 showed an 87% reduction in the intima of aortic arch compared to the intima of thoracic aorta.
source: While Aff3ir-ORF1 and Aff3 showed comparable expression levels in the intima of aortic arch and thoracic aorta of mice, the expression of Aff3ir-ORF2 showed an 87% reduction in the intima of aortic arch compared to the intima of thoracic aorta (Figure 1B and C), suggesting that Aff3ir-ORF2 may be a novel mechanosensitive protein that responds to disturbed shear stress.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: Aff3ir-ORF2 may be a novel mechanosensitive protein that responds to disturbed shear stress.
source: While Aff3ir-ORF1 and Aff3 showed comparable expression levels in the intima of aortic arch and thoracic aorta of mice, the expression of Aff3ir-ORF2 showed an 87% reduction in the intima of aortic arch compared to the intima of thoracic aorta (Figure 1B and C), suggesting that Aff3ir-ORF2 may be a novel mechanosensitive protein that responds to disturbed shear stress.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential expression pattern of Aff3ir-ORF2 in regions with different shear stress.

claim: Enface immunofluorescence staining confirmed a marked reduction in Aff3ir-ORF2 expression in the inner curvature of aortic arch compared to both the outer curvature of aortic arch and the thoracic aorta.
source: Enface immunofluorescence staining confirmed a marked reduction in Aff3ir-ORF2 expression in the inner curvature of aortic arch compared to both the outer curvature of aortic arch and the thoracic aorta (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1D and E.

claim: The expression of Aff3ir-ORF2 was notably downregulated in athero-prone regions compared to that in the protective region in the outer curvature of the aortic arch.
source: We found that the expression of Aff3ir-ORF2, but not Aff3, was notably downregulated in athero-prone regions (the inner curvature of the aortic arch and bifurcation of the carotid artery) compared to that in the protective region in the outer curvature of the aortic arch (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Disturbed shear stress significantly reduced both the protein and mRNA levels of Aff3ir-ORF2 in MEFs.
source: Consistent with our in vivo findings, while disturbed shear stress increased the expression of Vcam1, a critical inflammatory marker of ECs (Nakashima et al., 1998), it significantly reduced both the protein and mRNA levels of Aff3ir-ORF2 (Figure 1G–I).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1G-I and citation to Nakashima et al., 1998.

claim: Aff3ir-ORF2 overexpression attenuated Icam1 expression induced by disturbed shear stress at both the protein and mRNA levels in MEFs.
source: Aff3ir-ORF2 overexpression attenuated Icam1 expression induced by disturbed shear stress at both the protein and mRNA levels (Figure 2A, B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2A, B, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Aff3ir-ORF2 overexpression reduced the protein level of Icam1 induced by disturbed shear stress in HUVECs.
source: Consistent with our previous results, Aff3ir-ORF2 overexpression reduced the protein level of Icam1 induced by disturbed shear stress in HUVECs (Figure 2C–D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2C-D.

claim: Aff3ir-ORF2 overexpression attenuated disturbed shear stress-induced expression of Vcam1, Il6, and Il1b in both MEFs and ECs.
source: Moreover, Aff3ir-ORF2 overexpression attenuated disturbed shear stress-induced expression of several inflammatory genes, including Vcam1, Il6, and Il1b, in both MEFs and ECs. (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: Aff3ir-ORF2 overexpression significantly reduced the release of Il6 and Il1b induced by disturbed shear stress.
source: As expected, while Aff3ir-ORF2 overexpression had little effect on the concentrations of Il6 and Il1b under ST condition, it significantly reduced their release induced by disturbed shear stress (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Mice infected with Ad-Aff3ir-ORF2 exhibited a significant decrease in lesion area in the LCAs compared to those infected with Ad-Scramble (23 ± 17% vs 63 ± 14%).
source: Mice infected with Ad-Aff3ir-ORF2 exhibited a significant decrease in lesion area in the LCAs compared to those infected with Ad-Scramble (23 ± 17% vs 63 ± 14%) (Figure 2F–H), with no obvious plaque formation observed in the right carotid arteries (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2F-H and Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Overexpression of Aff3ir-ORF2 attenuated disturbed flow-induced inflammatory responses, as evidenced by decreased Vcam1 expression in the endothelium of LCAs.
source: Overexpression of Aff3ir-ORF2 also attenuated disturbed flow-induced inflammatory responses, as evidenced by decreased Vcam1 expression in the endothelium of LCAs (Figure 2I–J).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2I-J.

claim: Aff3ir-ORF2 deficient MEFs displayed higher expression of inflammatory genes, including Icam1, Vcam1, and Il1b, compared to those in WT MEFs, under disturbed flow stimulation.
source: Furthermore, we found that Aff3ir-ORF2 deficient MEFs displayed higher expression of inflammatory genes, including Icam1, Vcam1, and Il1b, compared to those in WT MEFs, under disturbed flow stimulation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Aff3ir-ORF2 deficiency accelerated the development of atherosclerosis in the entire aorta, AA, and TA.
source: En face Oil-Red O staining indicated that Aff3ir-ORF2 deficiency accelerated the development of atherosclerosis in the entire aorta, AA, and TA. (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3B and C.

claim: Aff3ir-ORF2 deletion increased the lesion area and lipid deposition in the aortic roots of Apoe-/- mice without altering the collagen fiber content.
source: Furthermore, Aff3ir-ORF2 deletion increased the lesion area and lipid deposition in the aortic roots of Apoe-/- mice without altering the collagen fiber content (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: Aff3ir-ORF2 deletion increased Vcam1 expression in the aortic roots of Apoe-/- mice.
source: We found that Aff3ir-ORF2 deletion increased Vcam1 expression in the aortic roots of Apoe-/- mice (Figure 3H, I), indicating that the atherogenic effects of Aff3ir-ORF2 deletion may result from endothelial inflammation.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3H and I.

claim: The atherogenic effects of Aff3ir-ORF2 deletion may result from endothelial inflammation.
source: We found that Aff3ir-ORF2 deletion increased Vcam1 expression in the aortic roots of Apoe-/- mice (Figure 3H, I), indicating that the atherogenic effects of Aff3ir-ORF2 deletion may result from endothelial inflammation.
evidence: This is inferred from the increased Vcam1 expression, a marker of endothelial inflammation.

claim: There were no significant differences between Apoe-/- and Apoe-/-Aff3ir-ORF2-/- mice in body weight or triglyceride, total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, and HDL cholesterol levels.
source: Additionally, there were no significant differences between the two groups in body weight or triglyceride, total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, and HDL cholesterol levels (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B), indicating that the atherogenic effect of Aff3ir-ORF2 silencing is unlikely to be related to lipid metabolism.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: The atherogenic effect of Aff3ir-ORF2 silencing is unlikely to be related to lipid metabolism.
source: Additionally, there were no significant differences between the two groups in body weight or triglyceride, total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, and HDL cholesterol levels (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B), indicating that the atherogenic effect of Aff3ir-ORF2 silencing is unlikely to be related to lipid metabolism.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of differences in lipid metabolism markers.

claim: RNA sequencing identified 1167 upregulated and 310 downregulated genes in the Aff3ir-ORF2-/- group, with a criterion of 1.5-fold change and p<0.05.
source: We identified 1167 upregulated and 310 downregulated genes in the Aff3ir-ORF2-/- group, with a criterion of 1.5-fold change and p<0.05 (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: GO analysis showed that differentially expressed genes were mainly enriched in processes, including leukocyte cell-cell adhesion, regulation of cell−cell adhesion, and leukocyte activation involved in immune response.
source: GO analysis showed that these genes were mainly enriched in processes, including leukocyte cell-cell adhesion, regulation of cell−cell adhesion, and leukocyte activation involved in immune response (Figure 4C), which is highly consistent with the phenotypes observed in Aff3ir-ORF2-/- mice.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Interferon regulatory factor 5 (Irf5) and Irf8 were identified as key upstream regulators.
source: Interferon regulatory factor 5 (Irf5) and Irf8 were identified as key upstream regulators (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Coimmunoprecipitation assays indicated that endogenous Aff3ir-ORF2 could bind to both Irf5 and Irf8.
source: Coimmunoprecipitation assays indicated that endogenous Aff3ir-ORF2 could bind to both Irf5 and Irf8 (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Silencing Irf5, but not Irf8, blunted the upregulation of inflammatory genes, including Icam1, Vcam1, Il6, and Il1b.
source: Notably, silencing Irf5, but not Irf8, blunted the upregulation of inflammatory genes, including Icam1, Vcam1, Il6, and Il1b (Figure 4F), suggesting that Irf5 was the predominant factor mediating the anti-inflammatory effects of Aff3ir-ORF2 in the context of disturbed shear stress.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Irf5 was the predominant factor mediating the anti-inflammatory effects of Aff3ir-ORF2 in the context of disturbed shear stress.
source: Notably, silencing Irf5, but not Irf8, blunted the upregulation of inflammatory genes, including Icam1, Vcam1, Il6, and Il1b (Figure 4F), suggesting that Irf5 was the predominant factor mediating the anti-inflammatory effects of Aff3ir-ORF2 in the context of disturbed shear stress.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects of Irf5 and Irf8 silencing.

claim: Irf5 silencing significantly inhibited the upregulation of Icam1 protein levels induced by Aff3ir-ORF2 deficiency under disturbed shear stress.
source: Consistently, we found that Irf5 silencing significantly inhibited the upregulation of Icam1 protein levels induced by Aff3ir-ORF2 deficiency under disturbed shear stress (Figure 4G and H).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4G and H.

claim: Aff3ir-ORF2 deficiency significantly increased the expression of Irf5-targeted genes, including Icam1, Ccl5, and Cxcl10.
source: However, we found that Aff3ir-ORF2 deficiency significantly increased the expression of Irf5-targeted genes (predicted by the ChEA3 database), including Icam1, Ccl5, and Cxcl10 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Irf5 was predominantly localized in the cytoplasm under static conditions, but exhibited obvious nuclear localization when exposed to disturbed shear stress.
source: Subcellular fractionation assays indicated that Irf5 was predominantly localized in the cytoplasm under static conditions, but exhibited obvious nuclear localization when exposed to disturbed shear stress (Figure 4I and J).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4I and J.

claim: Nuclear localization of Irf5 increased with Aff3ir-ORF2 deficiency.
source: While the total expression of Irf5 was barely affected by Aff3ir-ORF2 deficiency or overexpression, nuclear localization of Irf5 increased with Aff3ir-ORF2 deficiency (Figure 4I and J).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4I and J.

claim: Aff3ir-ORF2 overexpression significantly decreased the transcriptional activity of Irf5.
source: Aff3ir-ORF2 overexpression significantly decreased the transcriptional activity of Irf5 (Figure 4K).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4K.

claim: Aff3ir-ORF2 acts as an endogenous inhibitor of Irf5 and exerts anti-inflammatory effects by retaining Irf5 in the cytosol.
source: In summary, these results suggested that Aff3ir-ORF2 acts as an endogenous inhibitor of Irf5 and exerts anti-inflammatory effects by retaining Irf5 in the cytosol.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined results showing Aff3ir-ORF2 binding to Irf5, affecting its localization and transcriptional activity.

claim: Irf5 deletion resulted in an approximately 60% reduction in plaque area in the LCAs of Apoe-/- mice.
source: After a 4 wk high-fat diet challenge, Irf5 deletion resulted in an approximately 60% reduction in plaque area in the LCAs of Apoe-/- mice (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: Irf5 deletion attenuated endothelial activation, as evidenced by reduced Vcam1 expression in the endothelium of LCAs.
source: In addition, Irf5 deletion attenuated endothelial activation, as evidenced by reduced Vcam1 expression in the endothelium of LCAs (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: Irf5 deletion almost completely abolished the differences in plaque area and Vcam1 expression between Apoe-/- and Apoe-/-Aff3ir-ORF2-/- mice.
source: Notably, although Apoe-/-Aff3ir-ORF2-/- mice exhibited an increased plaque area in the LCAs compared to Apoe-/- mice, Irf5 deletion almost completely abolished these differences, reducing both the plaque area and Vcam1 expression in the endothelium of the LCAs (Figure 5A–D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5A-D.

claim: Aff3ir-ORF2 deficiency-induced atherosclerosis is mediated by endothelial Irf5.
source: These findings provide in vivo evidence that Aff3ir-ORF2 deficiency-induced atherosclerosis is mediated by endothelial Irf5.
evidence: This is inferred from the rescue of the atherosclerotic phenotype by Irf5 deletion.

claim: Endothelial-specific Aff3ir-ORF2 overexpression significantly reduced the Oil-red O-positive lesion area in the whole aortas of Apoe-/- mice (19 ± 5% vs 54 ± 8%).
source: However, compared to the negative control, endothelial-specific Aff3ir-ORF2 overexpression significantly reduced the Oil-red O-positive lesion area in the whole aortas of Apoe-/- mice (19 ± 5% vs 54 ± 8%) (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6B and C.

claim: Endothelial-specific Aff3ir-ORF2 overexpression reduced the lesion area and lipid deposition in the aortic roots of Apoe-/- mice without altering the collagen fiber content.
source: Moreover, endothelial-specific Aff3ir-ORF2 overexpression reduced the lesion area and lipid deposition in the aortic roots of Apoe-/- mice without altering the collagen fiber content (Figure 6D and E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6D and E.

claim: Aff3ir-ORF2 overexpression effectively suppressed Vcam1 expression in the endothelium of the aortic roots of Apoe-/- mice.
source: In addition, Aff3ir-ORF2 overexpression effectively suppressed Vcam1 expression in the endothelium of the aortic roots of Apoe-/- mice (Figure 6F and G).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6F and G.

claim: Supplementation with Aff3ir-ORF2 was effective in preventing atherosclerosis development.
source: Collectively, these results suggest that supplementation with Aff3ir-ORF2 was effective in preventing atherosclerosis development.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined results showing reduced lesion area and inflammatory markers.

claim: Disturbed shear stress significantly reduces Aff3ir-ORF2 expression in athero-prone regions.
source: We demonstrate that disturbed shear stress significantly reduces Aff3ir-ORF2 expression in athero-prone regions.
evidence: This is supported by data from multiple experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: Aff3ir-ORF2 exerts potent anti-inflammatory and anti-atherosclerotic effects in Apoe-/- mice.
source: Using three distinct mouse models with manipulated Aff3ir-ORF2 expression, we demonstrate that Aff3ir-ORF2 exerts potent anti-inflammatory and anti-atherosclerotic effects in Apoe-/- mice.
evidence: This is supported by data from multiple experiments shown in Figures 2, 3, 5, and 6.

claim: Interferon regulatory factor 5 (Irf5) mediates inflammatory responses associated with Aff3ir-ORF2 deficiency.
source: RNA sequencing revealed that interferon regulatory factor 5 (Irf5), a key regulator of inflammatory processes, mediates inflammatory responses associated with Aff3ir-ORF2 deficiency.
evidence: This is supported by RNA sequencing data and functional experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: Aff3ir-ORF2 interacts with Irf5, promoting its retention in the cytoplasm, thereby inhibiting the Irf5-dependent inflammatory pathways.
source: Aff3ir-ORF2 interacts with Irf5, promoting its retention in the cytoplasm, thereby inhibiting the Irf5-dependent inflammatory pathways.
evidence: This is supported by coimmunoprecipitation and subcellular fractionation data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Irf5 knockdown in Aff3ir-ORF2 deficient mice almost completely rescues the aggravated atherosclerotic phenotype.
source: Notably, Irf5 knockdown in Aff3ir-ORF2 deficient mice almost completely rescues the aggravated atherosclerotic phenotype.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Endothelial-specific Aff3ir-ORF2 supplementation using the CRISPR/Cas9 system significantly ameliorated endothelial activation and atherosclerosis.
source: Moreover, endothelial-specific Aff3ir-ORF2 supplementation using the CRISPR/Cas9 system significantly ameliorated endothelial activation and atherosclerosis.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Disturbed shear stress-induced endothelial atherogenic responses are pivotal in the initiation and progression of atherosclerosis.
source: Disturbed shear stress-induced endothelial atherogenic responses are pivotal in the initiation and progression of atherosclerosis, contributing to the uneven distribution of atherosclerotic lesions.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by the overall study findings.

claim: Aff3ir-ORF2 has potential as a valuable therapeutic approach for treating atherosclerosis.
source: These findings elucidate a novel role for Aff3ir-ORF2 in mitigating endothelial inflammation and atherosclerosis by acting as an inhibitor of Irf5, highlighting its potential as a valuable therapeutic approach for treating atherosclerosis.
evidence: This is speculative based on the study findings.

claim: Aff3ir-ORF2 knockout increased Vcam1 expression in the endothelium but had a minimal effect on collagen deposition within the plaques.
source: Notably, while Aff3ir-ORF2 knockout increased Vcam1 expression in the endothelium and enlarged the plaque area in the aortic roots, it had a minimal effect on collagen deposition within the plaques.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Irf5 expression is relatively low in VSMCs.
source: A previous study has shown minimal colocalization between Irf5 and the VSMC marker, α-smooth muscle actin, in aortic root lesions of Apoe-/- mice (Seneviratne et al., 2017), indicating a relatively low Irf5 expression level in VSMCs.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Seneviratne et al., 2017.

claim: Aff3ir-ORF2 likely exerts its anti-inflammatory effects primarily through endothelial Irf5.
source: Consequently, Aff3ir-ORF2 likely exerts its anti-inflammatory effects primarily through endothelial Irf5.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential expression of Irf5 in different cell types and the effects of endothelial-specific Aff3ir-ORF2 overexpression.

claim: Endothelial-specific Aff3ir-ORF2 overexpression reduced the aortic plaque area, but had minimal effects on collagen deposition.
source: Consistently, endothelial-specific Aff3ir-ORF2 overexpression reduced the aortic plaque area, but had minimal effects on collagen deposition.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Disturbed shear stress transcriptionally downregulated the expression of Aff3ir.
source: Additionally, we found that disturbed shear stress transcriptional downregulated the expression of Aff3ir.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The protein levels of Aff3ir-ORF2, but not those of Aff3ir-ORF1, were reduced by disturbed shear stress.
source: However, the protein levels of Aff3ir-ORF2, but not those of Aff3ir-ORF1, were reduced by disturbed shear stress.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Different translation mechanisms may be involved in the production of Aff3ir-ORF1/2.
source: Since both Aff3ir-ORF1 and Aff3ir-ORF2 are derived from Aff3ir, different translation mechanisms may be involved in the production of Aff3ir-ORF1/2.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the differential protein expression patterns.

claim: Elevated Irf5 expression and nuclear localization have been observed in macrophages within plaques of Apoe-/- mice.
source: Elevated Irf5 expression and nuclear localization have been observed in macrophages within plaques of Apoe-/- mice (Seneviratne et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Seneviratne et al., 2017.

claim: Irf5 drives macrophages towards a pro-inflammatory state, thereby affecting plaque stability.
source: Irf5 has been demonstrated to drive macrophages towards a pro-inflammatory state, thereby affecting plaque stability (Seneviratne et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Seneviratne et al., 2017.

claim: Global or myeloid cell-specific deletion of Irf5 stabilizes atherosclerotic plaques by suppressing the inflammatory phenotypes of macrophages.
source: Global or myeloid cell-specific deletion of Irf5 stabilizes atherosclerotic plaques by suppressing the inflammatory phenotypes of macrophages (Leipner et al., 2021; Seneviratne et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Leipner et al., 2021 and Seneviratne et al., 2017.

claim: Disturbed shear stress is sufficient to induce Irf5 nuclear translocation and activation in ECs.
source: Our study provides evidence that disturbed shear stress is sufficient to induce Irf5 nuclear translocation and activation in ECs.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Irf5 knockdown in ECs significantly reduced disturbed flow-induced plaque formation in LCAs.
source: Furthermore, Irf5 knockdown in ECs significantly reduced disturbed flow-induced plaque formation in LCAs.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Targeting endothelial Irf5 may be an effective strategy for combating the early stages of atherosclerosis.
source: These findings suggest that targeting endothelial Irf5 may be an effective strategy for combating the early stages of atherosclerosis.
evidence: This is speculative based on the study findings.

claim: Nanoparticle-delivered siRNA targeting Irf5 in macrophages promotes inflammation resolution, improves infarct healing, and attenuates post-myocardial infarction remodeling.
source: For example, nanoparticle-delivered siRNA targeting Irf5 in macrophages promotes inflammation resolution, improves infarct healing, and attenuates post-myocardial infarction remodeling (Courties et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Courties et al., 2014.

claim: Manipulating Irf5 protein levels through the E3 ubiquitin ligase, Trim21, has been explored as a strategy for modulating its activity.
source: Additionally, manipulating Irf5 protein levels through the E3 ubiquitin ligase, Trim21, has been explored as a strategy for modulating its activity (Lazzari et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lazzari et al., 2014.

claim: Endothelium-specific supplementation with Aff3ir-ORF2 effectively attenuated endothelial activation and reduced the atherosclerotic plaque area in Apoe-/- mice.
source: Importantly, endothelium-specific supplementation with Aff3ir-ORF2 effectively attenuated endothelial activation and reduced the atherosclerotic plaque area in Apoe-/- mice, suggesting that targeting endothelial Irf5 activation with Aff3ir-ORF2 holds promise for the treatment of atherosclerosis.
